title: No driver update policy, or approvals left pending
when: !Facts.DriverUpdatePolicies.Any(p => p.Assignments.Any()) || Facts.DriverUpdatePolicies.Any(p => p.PendingApprovalDays != null && p.PendingApprovalDays > params.maxPendingDays)

maxPendingDays.text: Days a driver approval may sit unactioned

messages.businessImpact: Driver and firmware updates carry security fixes as well as stability fixes, and where approval is manual the queue tends to be nobody's job.
remediation: Create a driver update policy, using automatic approval for the broad population.
Where manual approval is deliberate, put a recurring review in someone's calendar.
messages.cannotSee: Whether a policy exists and is assigned is read. How long a driver has been waiting for approval is not: the approval queue is a call of its own that this release does not make, so the second half of this rule reports nothing and a tenant with a manual policy and a year of pending drivers reads as covered. The policy's approval type is worth checking by hand where one exists.
